A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the CAPC-CG corpus and annotation pipeline. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and can be matched despite renumbering and substantial appendix expansion.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation validation, inter-annotator agreement, classification experiments in Tables 4–6, and temporal and topical corpus analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds supervised model benchmarks, detailed classification error analyses, topic-assignment validation, and corpus statistics.

M1.justification: The five-color scheme, two-stage classification, expert annotation and GPT-4o-mini fine-tuning, and hybrid segmentation procedure are retained. The newly emphasized 'expert-directed LLM annotation' method describes the existing pipeline; expanded implementation descriptions and additional comparison models do not establish a changed proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions cover Chinese central-government laws, administrative regulations, and ministerial rules from 1949–2023, with the same segmentation and two-level classification tasks. Additional benchmarks retain this coverage. Revised document counts and benchmark splits concern sample quantities and protocols, while Appendix K documents the existing topic analysis.

E2.justification: v2 adds supervised BERT-base-Chinese, Qwen2.5-7B, and Llama-3-8B comparisons at both classification levels in Appendix F, Tables 7–9. The original SVM, XGBoost, DeepSeek-V3, Qwen3-235B, and GPT-4o-mini comparisons remain. This substantially broadens the evaluated comparator families and adaptation methods.

E3.justification: Appendix E introduces distinct protocols for the added supervised benchmarks: Level-1 uses 600 balanced training examples, 300 balanced validation examples, and 1,901 naturally distributed test examples; Level-2 uses 1,200 training examples and a balanced 400-example validation/evaluation split without a separate test set. These settings differ from the retained main GPT-4o-mini setup and limit direct comparisons across training regimes.

E4.justification: Appendix H adds extensive error analyses for both classification levels, including confusion frequencies and bilingual failure cases. Appendix K adds topic-model checks using BERTopic and human validation on 200 paragraphs. These provide substantial diagnostic and validation evidence beyond v1's aggregate scores and descriptive corpus analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the three-round Fleiss' kappa results and report benchmark point estimates without seeds, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v2 clarifies independent coding and non-identical 500-item batches for the existing agreement plot, but adds no new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial benchmark results, including BERT-base-Chinese kappa values of 0.817 for Level-1 and 0.800 for Level-2, plus error distributions, 92% topic-assignment agreement, and detailed corpus distributions. The document total changes from 337,056 to 337,038. Original GPT-4o-mini headline scores remain unchanged; the added benchmarks do not establish a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: No new mathematical definitions, formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs are introduced. The segmentation cost calculations are retained. Expanded discussion of adaptive political economy and annotation principles is conceptual rather than a formal theoretical development.

C1.justification: The central corpus, five-color typology, coverage, and reliability claims remain. v2 additionally presents the existing expert-directed annotation workflow as an explicitly proposed and validated methodological contribution in the abstract and introduction, extending v1's emphasis on releasing a corpus and hybrid labeling pipeline.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands explanations of classification failures, particularly sanctioning authority versus prohibition and flexible implementation versus ambiguity, and argues that the task remains unsaturated. It adds a Water Resources interpretation and acknowledges the lack of a separate Level-2 test set. The limitations discussion also changes to reflect the broader, still non-exhaustive benchmark.

D1.justification: Appendix E newly documents GPT-4o-mini fine-tuning settings, output normalization, traditional-model features and hyperparameters, and detailed supervised/QLoRA configurations. Appendices J and K disclose annotator qualifications, training and compensation, and topic-model construction and assignment procedures. These substantially improve documentation; the repository link and previously documented segmentation implementation remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including Ang (2024), Blinder et al. (2008), and Merola and Singh (2025), and more explicitly positions expert-directed annotation against approaches treating LLMs as replacements for experts. DeepSeek-V3 and Qwen3 technical-report references are removed although their evaluated baselines remain. The main relationship to adaptive policy communication and existing corpus research is retained.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, contribution narrative, corpus-composition section, and future-directions discussion are substantially reworked. Technical material is reorganized through an appendix roadmap, the database description is condensed in the main text, and previously Chinese-only annotation prompts receive English translations. These changes extend beyond descriptions of the added experiments.

P2.justification: All eight figure images are retained, with changes to captions and placement; the overall workflow moves to the appendix. The database schema moves from main-text Table 3 to appendix Table 10. New extended-benchmark Tables 7–9 and descriptive Tables 11–13 substantially expand the table presentation and reorganize the document layout.

improvement.justification: The added training details, supervised baselines, and failure analyses improve reproducibility and scrutiny of results that v1 documented sparsely. The net gain is limited by unequal benchmark training regimes and reuse of Level-2 validation data for evaluation. New inconsistencies also remain: Table 1 includes Neutral paragraphs while Section 3.1 says they were removed, and Appendix H's Level-2 class accuracies conflict with Tables 5 and 9.
